equivalence.construction: Both hypothetical latent worlds use the same complete recorded copy-generator output. One stipulates object-name meaning; the other attributes strings to mechanical repetition without object-name meaning. Their observed labels, body strings and fixed metadata are identical by construction.
equivalence.proof: Every seven-model score, six increment and reference tail is a deterministic function of these observed strings/metadata. Both worlds point to one shared statistic computation, hence observationally identical for this evidence. This is an identifiability counterexample, not another null mechanism that should test negative.
limitations: Prefix counts are not independent samples; eight prefixes share each of 256 generator runs.
Binding hashes commit to source and state hashes rather than pretending to be a second raw manuscript.
No actual object truth, images, new language or historical causal evidence is supplied.
Does not establish that either latent mechanism actually generated Voynich text.
